ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 rider-cancellation fee under NS-4; no refund or waiver; advise the rider via RydeHELP that any discretionary goodwill review is a matter for Ryde under NS-7.
ruling.reasoning: The fee in dispute is the $6.61 cancellation fee, and the record settles the branch: cancelled_by = rider at 08:46:40, 6 min 40 s (400 s) after acceptance at 08:40:00 [F4][F7]. Under NS-0 the rider-cancellation branch is the only route into the NS clauses, and it is an instant booking, so the applicable test is NS-4 [F4][F7][NS-0][NS-4]. NS-4 charges nothing only if the rider cancels within 3 minutes of matching; 400 s exceeds 180 s, so the $6.61 stands as recorded on the fare record [F4][F7][NS-4]. The rider's fairness argument — that the driver "had not even arrived" — is contradicted by the system records, which override statements: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup and stayed within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap, and was stationary 41 m from the pickup from 08:42:00 to 08:46:40 [F2][F3][F6][NS-4]. Her own message at 08:45 — "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" — is a rider-side change of mind, not a driver fault, and the driver had already reported his position in chat at 08:42 [F9][F10][NS-4]. I read the two-message chat (both timestamped) and the driver's post-trip statement; the driver's statement that he "was parked at the pickup for minutes" is consistent with, and in any event subordinate to, the GPS/timeline records [F11][F12][F2][F3]. No NS-1 no-show fee is being justified here: the charge rests on the rider's own cancellation, though the same records show the driver's on-site presence if that branch were tested [F4][F6][NS-1][NS-0]. Because the cancellation is chargeable at 400 s and no refund flows from any clause, the amount is $0.00 (no computation: the fee is validated, not reduced) [F4][F7][NS-4]. The rider's profile (0 upheld no-show disputes) is not used against her and is not decisive either way [F16][NS-4]. No safety issue arises on the screen: I read chat #1 and chat #2, the driver's written statement and the complaint, and found no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1].

rejected_claims.reason: No-show clauses are indeed not the operative basis (conceded), and the assertion that nothing shows the rider at the pickup is beside the point — F4 establishes the fee on the rider's own cancellation outside the 3-minute window, so the claim does not defeat the charge under NS-4 [F4][F7][NS-0][NS-4].

Correct that Ryde publishes no driver-late free-cancellation rule and NS-8 is information-only; but that argument cannot reduce the fee — acceptance at 08:40:00 to cancellation at 08:46:40 is 400 s, beyond the 3-minute window, so the $6.61 is chargeable under NS-4 and NS-7 discretion is a matter for Ryde, not this ruling [F4][F7][NS-4][NS-7].
The driver's presence facts are accepted but added nothing to the fee's basis: the charge rests on the rider-cancellation branch, and F1/F6 were not needed to sustain it [F1][F6][F4][NS-0][NS-4].
Accepted as consistent with the record (stationary 4 min 40 s, within 200 m for 5 min 15 s), but the NS-1 no-show fee is not what is charged; the $6.61 stands on NS-4 alone [F3][F2][F4][NS-1][NS-4].

Supported: the 08:42 chat places the driver at the pickup, and the rider's non-dispute of it removes any failure-to-notify claim; it corroborates but does not itself create the charge, which rests on NS-4 timing [F9][F4][NS-4].
